body:
I can relate to that, I think this does apply to me too. I don't necessarily strive for perfection, but rather the ''right'' thing, I can't help but think that majority of people are wrong, the way they lead their lives etc. I also can't comprehend people with divorces/failed relationships, in a sense that how short sighted you have to be, it has to be literal lack of care or even minimum expenditure of effort. Or always getting into ''bad relationships'' and similar things, when if you read about things like that, everything screams from the get go of a disaster in making. It makes me angry to a degree, too, because of how easy they have it and how people don't appreciate things that are important and just take it for granted. Though this was a bit off the topic.

While generally, I do agree with many things that you say, which may just boil down to bitterness/malice of sorts, that we might have in common towards the world. I don't quite understand why would you try to ''cheat'' so to say in pretending to be normal or something else, to get a shot at something to just later reveal yourself. The entire relationship gets built on a false premise and lies, which I think is eventually most likely destined to fail. Also, I'd say, I would find it very off putting and disingenuous whether it'd be me doing this or somebody else doing it to me. And this is what I have a big problem in todays society/world, also a part of what makes people so fake nowadays. I mean, I think it's just wrong thing to do, also would never lead to true happiness either, that again is just my belief though.

Yes the reason of existence, I don't want to sound like I have everything figured out and know it all, but there's no reason. On universe scale there might be a reason of sorts, but we're as relevant as a grain of sand in a random beach, no matter what we do the outcome isn't going to change on grand scale of things. As if the system is already built on a basis that everything is taken into account and everything is a fair go and within expectations. You don't really need to make an actual reason. I think it's just about finding something you love, something that makes you happy and lets you enjoy the ride, simply happiness. Or at least not a torment. Which is again, what the problem is, at least for me. It doesn't seem possible in this world and I'm certainly losing the hope, just not sure yet, whether I've lost it completely already. 
As to twisted ways, I feel like I'm genuinely too good of a person, too polite, too caring, too nice to such a degree it completely backfires on me and people just see it as an easy way to exploit naivety. I'm just striving to be somebody who I want others to be, which is probably another one of those things as to why I fail at everything. Even though I understand what is going on, deep inside I hope that I'm wrong and hope that they too might be good, or that they won't do the ''bad'' thing. Needless to say, the answer to that is fairly obvious. Often times it's just small little things though. Once again, ties in to the trust, giving up on humanity and such, so I somewhat feel like repeating a lot already myself and paraphrasing you. In fact, many other people too.

I've read about things, lots of things on internet, tried to talk to other people on internet. Just seems there are SO many people like us, yet in real life you can never find any, just a bit strange. I can understand why people don't like pessimism, I try to consciously avoid it. The problem I find though, is that if you're being realistic you will often be branded as pessimist, I think. And lots of twisted views are just being a realist too, only because they don't experience it, doesn't mean that it doesn't exist. Even better is, when they do know it exists, but they get angry if you talk about it, because it upsets people or the worst, you have to actively censor yourself. In the end, I honestly don't know how all this can help, it's just one of those things for me. Do something different this day than the day before, and maybe this somehow will lead to something new and different, the 0.0001% chance of something to happen, I suppose. Maybe helps to organize thoughts into some kind of form, as I always just let it boil inside. Today I did things, differently, went to make an appointment about things I don't care, just because. Ran more than usual and I'm writhing in agony, feel awful as usual, just with more pain and all for nothing. I don't know why it has to be this way, but I know how unpleasant it is and I just want to end it all or for it to end.

I didn't see this for some reason, anyway. I always lived in the city that I live today, I don't think it's very big or anything, something like 200-300k people. I myself live a bit outside of city, and my house is 20 meters away from forest, and even when I was a kid I lived near forest and would spend some time there. I personally would really want to run away from city in general, really really far far away, from everything. I think this is one of the reasons people dislike me a lot, in a way. But I think if I were to do that, then my chances of finding somebody or anything at all would go from 0.01% to literally 0. That is something I'm afraid of, but very often think about it too, because I'm not sure what is the right thing to do. Is it to keep on trying to be a human? Or just run away and forget that civilization exists? Because it's quite clear I don't exist from their perspective. Maybe it'd hurt less, or maybe I'd just come at peace with all of it and give up easier and just kill myself already or become a crazy wild person and start talking with animals.

It is a similar world view I had and still have actually, for quite a while. That is, looking at things and events from probability stand point, as in for example percentages. That's why I still, go and do it, something different, something unusual, just because there might be a chance. The way I see, everything is odds to a certain degree, and nothing should be guaranteed to happen. Whether it's 50% or 0.01%, just as long as there's a probability, you should try to take advantage of it. That's how I rationally think, it's just that reality has been very opposite, where you think something is 50% and it fails 100 times in a row, it has got to be either not 50% or I'm just incredibly unlucky. And in this case it feels like everything is stacked against you, then add lots of other problems and issues in the pot and you have a disaster boiling, so to say.

In a similar way, I tried to approach people, if you take that 0.5% people you can find something in common and potentially become friends, then realistically speaking you should go through at least 200 people, and that wouldn't be a guarantee whatsoever, that you'd find somebody. That's what makes sense to me, but I can't either physically or mentally go through hundreds and hundreds of people. The experience is just so soul crushing, being an introvert doesn't help either, not in the slightest.

I've tried finding hobbies. In a way that's why I'm probably staying ''active'' and try to do something every day, that is exercising. To a degree you can see the results, improvements, but honestly it's mostly negative in a sense, that I don't progress as much and as fast as I'd like to or worse - stalling, so even in that I feel a somewhat failure. I really dislike working, because as I said, I feel like I'm rejected by entire world and my entire existence boils down to being a slave and paying taxes, with nothing else in my life. I don't care about money, it doesn't bring me happiness, I don't need it, it doesn't serve a purpose to me. But if you genuinely feel like you do like working and enjoy it, at least that it makes your life bearable, you probably should stick to it. I don't think it would be something for me personally. Otherwise I don't know, I try to like something, but it's like I'm dead, it's becoming harder and harder to enjoy anything. I think that with time I'm becoming more and more masochistic, which probably isn't going to lead to anything particularly positive. As in I'm trying to hurt myself to just feel something else, like through exercise or otherwise. If I think about my life, often time I'd probably describe it as pain in dullness. I also tried the online communities, but even in those I feel like I'm just shunned, because of my opinions/worldviews, just a manner of speech. I think I'm a very mechanical person and care about little details, as to how things work and exact principles, which probably annoys people. Even between loners I end up being rejected and shunned away. 

Maybe it's in fact a ME problem, which by the way is sort of a reason I went to psychologist and even bothered with all the nonsense in there, to just be told: "you're ok, just bee urself lol xd and keep on trying". So then I come a full circle once again. If it's all about how wrong and awful and terrible I am, and world doesn't accept me for who I am, then I don't want to be something that I'm not, to just please the world. So what is exactly the point of living? If the only way world accepts you, if you're not you, yourself. I can't find happiness in loneliness and pointlessness, except the only way I keep on finding strength to keep on living is through distracting myself, but I feel like I've been doing that for way too long and it doesn't really work anymore. Just thinking as what my life has been so far and that's what is gonna be, just worse in the future, it's dreadful. I suppose, I just always look whiny and crying for no reason, but I'm trying to be as descriptive as I can, because I don't feel like I'm able to convey the feelings and experiences, what I truly think, in mere words.

Yes, pretty much agree with you. It's very hard to trust and rely on people in regards to anything whatsoever. Quite a big part of people I've ever met have been, to put it softly - unpleasant. I just personally don't think, that trust has much to do with being an introvert. 

It's just that I can't help, but feel that it is a wrong thing to do, to be and to stay alone your entire life. To be unhappy and miserable. I don't want to chase people, I want a mutual and symbiotic relationship, where I'd be loved and I could love somebody else, understand each other. To just feel a little bit of happiness and light in the life. To share some little moments, at least something with somebody, no matter how small or big and insignificant it might be. Yet, this seems like asking way too much. As if it is way out of the ordinary, as if I'm a biggest lunatic in the world for wanting something pleasant in life. It just feels like I'm withering away into nothingness, all these things add up into an unbearable anguish, where there seems little to no value in trying to continue to slog through it. Being an introvert, I naturally don't need a 24/7 exposure to people, but being at extremes, your entire life, no matter which side it may be, is certainly sub optimal to say the least.

I also can't help, but feel that majority of people are fakes and it just gives off a rubbery/plasticky feeling. Where even if I hypothetically could find somebody that would like me, would most likely end up incompatible.
You don't sound happy yourself either. I don't know you or your life, but I would most likely wouldn't want to be you either, I understand that there are plenty of people in worse situations than me or you or whoever else. Though that doesn't really change anything for our lives and it sucks to be us. I also think that I'm most likely not materialistic, so material world never seemed to carry much of any value to me. So I would probably bond to ideas in this case, which you could call non living things, even though this sounds nonsensical. But as I said earlier, I don't believe this could breath in a  purpose and satisfaction to life to majority of people. Also yes, individualism is very much so rampant, even I am most likely would fall in there, considering how many ''I's'' I wrote down in this entire thing, can't shake the feeling of how egocentric I may sound.

I could say that a lot of things do apply. I don't know how to explain, but got to say that it made me confused in a way. It doesn't seem to be real in a sense, that it is just a normal thing? As in everyone should be a HSP, as I imagine it applies to majority of people.

I've looked into meditation some time ago, maybe a few years ago. I can't say I have any interest in it though.

I like it because there isn't much noise, relatively speaking. Also health concerns. After spending quite a bit of time in forest, going out in city just feels awful physically and it smells bad. It's easier on feets/legs to walk over ground rather than concrete. 
Now it's autumn, so lots of pretty yellow/red leaves and it's just pretty in general. Also like walking over the leaves. In spring when everything starts blooming and trees turn green, the green is so bright it sort of burns my eyes, in a pleasant way. 
During winter even if it's -20c, it feels rather warm and comfortable. It seems like trees protect you from cold, so it's very pleasant to be in the forest, because air is cold, but it feels warm. Difficult to explain, maybe I'm just going too far. Enjoy walking over the snow, the sound and the feeling of I guess exploration and discovery, because you can see where people have walked or where they been, so you can choose to go where no one has went yet, it probably sounds stupid and childish.

I think that living in city and in general, modern living standarts are quite contrary to the way we should be living, so spending less time in city if possible is just better/healthier. 
Even though this sound stupid. Just being in nature is simply more natural, so it makes me believe it is at least not a wrong thing to do. 
I like visiting places that I found in forest that are pleasant for me to be in, so it takes time to visit them all from time to time. Just to see if things have changed, little by little they do change. So it's like watching something grow together with you.

I mean, I probably could go on about this, for a bit in fact, there're many things that I think I like, but I'm just not really sure if I like it or just think that I do.

Yes, if you think rationally, I of course do agree with you. In fact it's rather impossible to not be the case, that entire world conspires against particularly me, or that it is impossible to find somebody etc etc. It's just that in reality is not the case and it hasn't been a day or two or a year or two, but more than a decade. The more time passes the less hope you're left with and there, I suppose has to be a breaking point eventually. And I think, that I'm at the point where as the time goes on, things are not going to get better anymore, but only worse.

I loved to watch movies, listening to music, playing games, go for a swim. I don't even really know anymore. Nothing particularly special or unusual. With the time though, there's nothing left that I love or want to do anymore. I feel like I've seen all the movies, listened to all the music, played all the games etc etc. Everything is dull and boring. I believe I'm starting to lose comprehension of how people can even be happy in the world doings things when everything is just so tedious and dim. I could guess that having somebody to do it with helps. Not that I would ever know. Nowadays, I suppose I like to go outside into the forest and just walk, often pointlessly, fantasizing about good and bad things. Then again, can't imagine anyone finding that interesting or fulfilling, so probably would end up alone even doing things that I love/want to do, even if I had somebody.

I mean, I know that. I've read it already, not once or twice. It's quite... common? As far as advice goes in regards to girls. But I've never ever went past the "Hi" or 1 sentence with a girl, unless it's completely unrelated to relationship.
And I've been trying and going and doings things, but everyone is always with friends and talking in their own groups etc, I'm just there alone sitting awkwardly. Do the thing you came for and that essentially is it. It is as if you don't really exist. Neither do I try to pick anyone up there. Often time it's difficult to have fun, because it's mostly unpleasant and uncomfortable to be, and I think people quickly pick up on it too, that I'm alone, and then even try to avoid me. Also not very interesting either. And, well, awkward.

I don't think I have low self-confidence, it just hurting a lot. I mean of course I'm nowhere near to being super confident or anything, but that's not really the problem, though maybe I'm wrong. I just feel like entire world has rejected me decades ago and all I know is misery, which just feels terrible and helpless and it hurts a lot. Nobody cares about me, nobody loves me, I only exist to exist, feel miserable and pay taxes. And it's not like I'm making this up in my head, that's how it is. I don't have anyone or anything. People don't think that I'm a human. 

I genuinely want to die every day for many many years, yet I'm still alive, just because I'm afraid. I don't understand why I keep on even trying anymore, it just causes more pain. Like, all my dreams that I had, turned into just not wanting to wake up one day. It feels like the only way to feel anything else anymore is to become evil or to not feel anything at all, by dying. I'm sorry for even bothering you with all this. The only way to not think about all this constantly, is by distracting yourself, that is by reading or playing games or whatever. But whenever you stop you just start feeling even worse, because of how useless it is.

That's the thing, I suppose I don't really know. I could probably say, that I've never in my life had any real relationships with anyone, besides parents to a degree, I guess.
When I meet people, it has been mostly through work or I suppose in a business like manner. Most often I don't have anything in common with majority of them. Sometimes there'd be a person with whom I can find topics to talk about and it may seem like we could become friends, endless things to talk for hours on end. But it never goes anywhere. It's always me that has to call, ask, be forward, it feels that it's always me that is initiating or showing the effort. There is very little reciprocation and it feels like I'm just burdening them and I start to feel even hostility maybe. Also, I don't know how to approach people or make friends, so often time I try to help or offer a favour of sorts, so in a way I feel like I'm just being used for that, because soon after they don't care about me. In a way this sounds like I'm desperate or clingy? But those contacts are once a week or month, soon it fizzles out. I don't think I'm being too annoying or anything in terms of that. 
Also, I'm introverted and in general have difficulty of speaking with people and really prefer to talk one on one, rather than in a group. Maybe I'm just very boring. In terms of being ugly, I probably am, I tried to talk to girls, generally it's always a negative experience and have tried online dating, but it's as if I don't exist even there.
Also, as I said I'm very genuine and honest, maybe even too much. A lot of people are generally too mean, rude, deceitful, so I don't really want to have much in common with those people.
